newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends up at 35.76/77 on poor dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends up at 35.76/77 on poor dlr demand.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended Monday at 35.76/77 per dollar in dull, range-bound trade after opening the day at 35.79/80, dealers said.
They said last week's trend -- poor dollar demand, good supplies and lack of active dollar purchases by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) continued to dog the market on Monday.
"It was overall a quiet market," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "There were lot of dollar sellers," he said.

The spot rupee saw a high of 35.76 and a low of 35.79 on Monday. The dollar looked up briefly in the afternoon when the RBI bought small lots of forward dollars but fell back to earlier levels as soon as the central bank's intervention ended, dealers said.
The rupee continued last week's trend of rising against the forward dollar. The six month annualised premium closed at 4.53 percent compared to the previous close of 4.97 percent.
The premiums rose by one to two paise, following RBI's forward dollar purchases, but reverted to earlier levels towards the close, dealers said.
